# Where the real names come from

Research log for growing `data/names-db.tsv`: every government (or government-registry) source of first names we looked for, what's in, and what's left. Last updated 2 October 2026.

**Now:** 529,563 single first names from official records in **18 countries**, plus ~249,000 generated by Lullabyte.

How it's built:

```
python3 scripts/fetch_world.py     # downloads every reachable source into raw/ (not committed)
python3 scripts/build_world.py     # reads them all into data/names-db.tsv
```

Rules applied to every source: one name per entry (compound names are split, see `scripts/single_names.py`), Latin script only (the music box and search need letters they can sound out), at least one vowel (drops initials like "Md", "Jr"), registry placeholders removed ("Baby", "Unknown", "Kein Vorname", "Recién nacido"…), patronymics removed ("…ovna", "…ovich"). Names that differ only by accent stay separate spellings (José, Jose).

Notes:
- **Chile** lists every name ever registered, so it adds a lot of rare and creative spellings (Yxarely, Waberly). They are real registrations. 171,000 names in the whole database were recorded for exactly one person.
- **Germany**: 114 of the ~1,090 files gave nothing usable. Most are Dortmund's linked-data JSON copies of CSVs we already read, plus two old `.xls` files.
- **Australia**: 21 Queensland "Top 100" files downloaded empty. Retrying would add little (top 100 only).

## 📜 Names from sacred texts

`data/scripture-names.json` (built by `scripts/build_scriptures.py`): **13,695 names**, each with its story and the texts it appears in. They load into the app as names with stories, so the religion filter, the new "named in ⟨text⟩" blank and the cards all use them.

| Texts | Source | Names | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bible: Torah, Hebrew Bible, New Testament** | STEPBible **TIPNR** (Tyndale House): every person named in the Bible, with gender, a one-line description and every verse | 1,703 (433 in the Torah) | CC BY 4.0 |
| Bible name meanings | **Hitchcock's Bible Names Dictionary** (1869) | 1,286 meanings | Public domain |
| **Mahabharata · Bhagavad Gita** | Sørensen's *Index to the Names in the Mahābhārata* (1904) · Mehendale's *Mahābhārata Cultural Index* | 6,535 (160 in the Gita) | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 |
| **Puranas · Ramayana** | Vettam Mani's *Purāṇic Encyclopaedia* · Dikshitar's *Purāṇa Index* | 6,236 Puranas · 326 Ramayana | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 |
| **Vedas** | Macdonell & Keith's *Vedic Index of Names and Subjects* (1912) | 692 | CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 |
| Gita text (to find which names it mentions) | gita/gita verse data | — | Unlicense |
| **Quran** | **Quranic Arabic Corpus** (Kais Dukes): every proper noun, with how often and where it appears | 89: 41 people, 10 places, 38 Quranic words given as names (Noor, Huda, Rahma…) | GPL (text: Tanzil) |

How they were cleaned:
- **Bible:** only the person's own name (translations sometimes reuse a name for someone else, like KJV "Lydia" for Lud); gender weighed by how often each person is mentioned (Noah the patriarch, not Noah daughter of Zelophehad); a name in Genesis–Deuteronomy is tagged Torah.
- **Hindu texts:** the five books also index rivers, kingdoms, rituals, metres and dishes, so only people, gods, sages and named beings are kept. When many share a name, the one with the longest entry is the famous one (Kṛṣṇa, not Kṛṣṇā). Aliases take the gender of who they name (Shiva's 1,000 names). Scholarly spelling becomes everyday spelling (Kṛṣṇa → Krishna, Śrī Rāma → Shri Rama), and Sanskrit stems get the form people say (Hanumat → Hanuman).
- **Quran:** the people are every person and angel named in the text (devils and Pharaoh's title left out), each with how many times and where they first appear.
- A name in two traditions (Adam in the Bible and the Quran) keeps both stories.
- ⚠️ The Sanskrit indexes are **non-commercial** (CC BY-NC-SA). Fine for a portfolio; not if Lullabyte ever makes money.

## 🇮🇱 Hebrew names from Israel

Israel's records are in Hebrew letters, usually without vowels, so `scripts/hebrew_names.py` turns each name into the Latin spelling people use, **without guessing**:
1. a known pairing: a Wikidata given name whose Hebrew label is that exact spelling (Noa, Yael, Hamutal), or the Bible's Hebrew form (STEPBible);
2. otherwise every way the letters can be read under modern Hebrew spelling rules (ו is "v" only at the start, א and ע carry vowels, the unwritten vowel is usually "a"; Arab families' names use Arabic sounds), **kept only if that spelling is already a real registered name** held by 20+ people, of the right sex, the most natural reading winning (Shira, Lior, Yuval, Matan, Khaled);
3. a short hand-checked list of the usual Israeli spelling for common names whose romanization doesn't follow the letters (Guy, Eyal, Meir, Shlomo, Hillel).

Names that can't be verified are left out. Spot-checks of the 300 most common names read the way Israelis spell them; some rare Arabic names are still off (סלטאן came out "Colten", not Sultan).

`data/hebrew-names.json` then adds **942 names with cards** (Hebrew spelling and how many Israeli babies got the name): **496 with Hebrew roots** (Hebrew by origin: Bible, a native-Hebrew Wikidata label, or the usual-spelling list) and **446 Israeli** (mostly given in Israel, whatever their origin, e.g. Russian and Ethiopian names). Search them with "with ⟨Hebrew / Israeli⟩ roots".

## 🇯🇵 🇰🇷 🇨🇳 Japanese, Korean and Chinese names

None of these governments publish name counts, so `scripts/build_east_asian.py` builds `data/east-asian-names.json` from open dictionaries of names and characters:

| | Source | Names | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Japanese** | **JMnedict** (EDRDG): every given name in Japan's largest open names dictionary, with its gender and every way it is written | **33,831 real names** | romanized as on Japanese passports (Yūki → Yuki); the spelling shown uses the characters most often used for that name, at its usual length (Haruto 春人, Sakura 咲良); meanings from **KANJIDIC2**, with name-friendly senses for common name kanji (博 "learned", not "Dr."); gender from JMnedict's tags, or official records where they're clear (Haruto, Riku: boys) |
| **Korean** | name syllables with their usual hanja, checked against **KANJIDIC2**'s Korean readings | **3,881** (real ones like Minjun, Seoyeon, Haeun marked real) | built the way Korean names are made, two syllables (민 敏 clever + 준 俊 talented = Minjun), in the official Revised Romanization; a girls' and a boys' syllable never mix |
| **Chinese** | ~150 common given-name characters, pinyin and meanings from **CC-CEDICT** (MDBG) | **9,857** (3,800+ registered somewhere, like Zihan, Xinyi, Yuxuan, marked real) | two characters (子 zǐ child + 涵 hán contain = Zihan), pinyin without tone marks in the name, with them in the story; doubled names (Tingting) for girls |

Where one spelling exists in two languages, it lives in one: Japanese first (real names), then Korean, then Chinese (Yui is Japanese, Minjun Korean). Search with "with ⟨Japanese / Korean / Chinese⟩ roots".

⚠️ JMnedict, KANJIDIC2 and CC-CEDICT are CC BY-SA 4.0 (share-alike), like the Brazil list.

## 🌍 Names sorted into their cultures

Most names reach the database through registries abroad (a Yoruba name recorded in the UK, a Tamil name in Canada), with no culture attached. `scripts/build_cultures.py` builds `data/culture-names.json`, which puts **32,000+ names into 123 cultures**, each also in a broad basket (African, South Asian, Slavic, Central Asian, Pacific, Nordic, Celtic, Indigenous American, Taiwanese Indigenous).

| Source | What it gives |
|---|---|
| **Wiktionary** (CC BY-SA 4.0), `scripts/fetch_wiktionary_names.py` | ~40,000 entries from 120 languages' "male / female / unisex given names" categories, with gender, and a meaning when the entry gives one (`meaning=`, a literal translation, the words it's built from, or the ordinary word the name is: Tamil அன்பு Anbu, "love") |
| **Wiktionary**, `scripts/fetch_name_meanings.py` | meanings from each name's own page ("from Igbo, literally 'God leads'") and from the word in its language (Swahili *baraka*, "blessing") |
| **Wikidata** (CC0) | 38,500 given names tagged with their language |
| hand-written (`names.js`) | 657 well-known names with meanings for baskets the sources barely cover: Zulu, Xhosa, Sotho, Tswana, Swahili, Akan day names, Somali, Ethiopian, Punjabi, Urdu, Pashtun, Thai, Tibetan, Nepali, Burmese, Khmer, Lao, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Hawaiian, Māori, Yoruba |

Names in other scripts get their usual Latin spelling: Wiktionary's recorded romanization; the official systems for Cyrillic (per language: Ukrainian г is h, Bulgarian щ is sht…), Greek, Armenian and Georgian; and for the Indian scripts (one shared table for Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam) every likely reading, keeping the one already registered somewhere (Gurpreet, Murugan, Karthikeyan, Lavanya, Arnab), else the usual conventions (Tamil Senthil, Sadasivan). Thai, Burmese, Khmer, Lao and Arabic-script names without a recorded romanization are left out.

Rules: a South Asian, African or Asian form of a name from far away (Tamil Moshe, from Hebrew) doesn't count as that culture's roots; one name can sit in several cultures (Amina: Hausa, Swahili, Somali); caste terms are removed.

Biggest baskets: Turkish 2,053, Icelandic 1,963, Albanian 1,489, Italian 1,486, Faroese 1,384, Estonian 1,165, Polish 1,085, Finnish 996, Serbian & Croatian 928, Hindi 817, Kazakh 772, Filipino 768, Bengali 592, Russian 456, Armenian 454, Greek 452, Persian 409, Yoruba 398, Vietnamese 330, Igbo 213, Gujarati 207, Malayali 199, Hawaiian 193, Tamil 146, Hausa 118, Māori 105, Telugu 102.

Country lists checked for this step, all top-10 to top-50 only (PDFs): Philippines (PSA), South Africa (Stats SA), Turkey (TÜİK), Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Armenia (Armstat), Hungary (KSH).

## ⏳ The time machine: every year, from official birth records

`data/years.json` (built by `scripts/build_years.py`) holds the top 12 girls' and boys' names of **every year** for 29 places, with each publisher's own rules kept beside the numbers, so a name that isn't listed reads "not published", never "0 babies".

| Place | Publisher | Years | Publication rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🇺🇸 United States | Social Security Administration | 1880–2025 | names given to fewer than 5 babies a year aren't published |
| 🇫🇷 France | INSEE (fichier des prénoms 2024) | 1900–2024 | counts rounded to the nearest 5; rare names grouped |
| 🇳🇴 Norway | Statistics Norway, table 10467 | 1945–2025 | names used by 200+ people; fewer than 4 a year hidden; counts before 1945 not given |
| 🇨🇦 Canada | Statistics Canada, table 17-10-0147-01 | 1991–2025 | small counts suppressed |
| 🏴 England & Wales | ONS | 1996–2025; top 100 every ten years 1904–1994 | 2 or fewer redacted; 1904–1994 ranks only |
| 🏴 Scotland | National Records of Scotland | 1974–2025 | every first forename |
| Northern Ireland | NISRA full list | 1997–2025 | fewer than 3 not shown |
| 🇮🇪 Ireland | CSO, VSA50 / VSA60 | 1964–2025 | 3 or more occurrences |
| 🇦🇹 Austria | Statistik Austria | 1984–2025 | before 2010, Austrian nationals only |
| 🇳🇿 New Zealand | Department of Internal Affairs | 1900–2025 | 10+ registrations a year; registration years |
| 🇦🇺 New South Wales | NSW Registry | 1952–2025 | ranked list only |
| 🇦🇺 Queensland | Queensland Registry of BDM (data.qld.gov.au) | 1960–2025 | top 100 only |
| 🇸🇪 Sweden | Statistics Sweden, TAB619 (to 2022) · Skatteverket, Namn på nyfödda (from 2023) | 1998–2025 | top 100 to 2022 with spellings grouped; Skatteverket's list from 2023, spellings apart |
| 🇵🇱 Poland | dane.gov.pl, Imiona nadawane dzieciom w Polsce (PESEL) | 2000–2025 | fewer than 5 hidden to 2012, fewer than 2 from 2013 |
| 🇩🇰 Denmark | Statistics Denmark, Navne til nyfødte | 1985–2025 | top 25 to 1992, top 50 from 1993; before 1996 Danish citizens only |
| 🇨🇭 Switzerland | Federal Statistical Office, DF_BEVNAT_PRENOMS (stats.swiss) | 2000–2025 | names given in the latest year, counted back to 2000 |
| Catalonia | Idescat, Noms dels nadons | 1997–2025 | top 100; accented and unaccented spellings counted together |
| 🇩🇪 Berlin | Berlin Open Data, Liste der häufigen Vornamen | 2012–2023 | one city, not Germany; first names only from 2017 |
| 🇳🇱 Netherlands | SVB, kindernamen | 2017–2025 | fewer than 10 hidden |
| 🇲🇩 Moldova | Public Services Agency (dataset.gov.md) | 2016–2023 | top 20–100 registered newborn names |
| 🇱🇺 Luxembourg | STATEC, La démographie luxembourgeoise en chiffres | 2022–2024 | top 5 only; spellings apart |
| 🇧🇬 Bulgaria | National Statistical Institute, Names in Bulgaria | 2012–2025 | top 20 to 2015, top 10 from 2016; Cyrillic kept |
| 🇧🇦 Federation of BiH | Federal Statistical Office (fzs.ba) | 2012–2025 | top 100 |
| 🇧🇦 Republika Srpska | Republika Srpska Institute of Statistics | 2024–2025 | ranks only: top 10 in 2024, top 4 in 2025; Cyrillic kept |
| 🇱🇻 Latvia | Central Statistical Bureau, 100 most popular newborn names | 1918–2026 in five-year periods | top 100, ranks only; before 1990 only people still in the register |
| 🇨🇱 Chile | Registro Civil (via guaguas) | 1920–2021 | every name, even once; series ended |
| 🇿🇦 South Africa | Stats SA, Recorded live births (P0305) | 2014–2024 | top 10 only |
| 🇧🇷 Brazil | IBGE, Censo 2010 names | decades of birth, before 1930 to 2000s | people alive at the 2010 census, top 20 |
| 🇫🇮 Finland | DVV Nimipalvelu | decades of birth, 1900s–2020s | people in the population register, all first names; fewer than 5 hidden |

How the hard ones were reached: **ssa.gov** and **data.govt.nz** block scripts, so their official files were opened in a browser and only each year's top names were kept (`raw/us-top20-2018-2025.tsv`, `raw/nz-top12-1900-2025.txt`). US 1880–2017 comes from the babynames R package, which is built from the same SSA files. **data.qld.gov.au** challenges scripts on its download links, so Queensland was read through the portal's own CKAN datastore API. Denmark's top 50 comes from the HTML endpoint behind dst.dk's "Top 50" selector, South Africa's top 10 from the tables inside each P0305 PDF, Moldova's from the yearly reports (PDF, DOCX, XLSX), and Catalonia's accented spellings (Martí, Adrià) from each name's Idescat page because the API drops accents.

Not ingested: **Belgium** (every statbel.fgov.be URL, file downloads included, returns a CAPTCHA page), **Philippines** (psa.gov.ph returns a Cloudflare challenge), **Argentina 2012–2024** (datosabiertos.renaper.gob.ar times out from here; the 1922–2015 RENAPER file `raw/ar-renaper-historico-nombres-1922-2015.zip` has full given names and counts by year but no sex column, so it can't be split into girls and boys without guessing), **Lithuania** (data.gov.lt and registrucentras.lt block this network), **Liechtenstein** (statistikportal.li and llv.li return a Cloudflare challenge; the XLSX needs a manual download), **Kosovo** (the Agency of Statistics' name search gives a top 5 per birth year 1940–2025 with girls and boys mixed, residents not registrations; its census report's most common name for each age 1–100 is in `data/census-names.json`), **Georgia** (the Public Service Development Agency's name statistics need a reCAPTCHA token and have no years; no newborn rankings on sda.gov.ge, justice.gov.ge or geostat.ge), **Iceland** (the PxWeb API only has names born in 2021 and population snapshots by age, no birth-year series or census tables), **Andorra** (the Observatori de la infància reports checked carry birth counts but no name rankings).

Montenegro's 2023 census names by age group and municipality (MONSTAT release 149/2024, names only) are kept apart in `data/census-names.json`, with Kosovo's 2024 census (most common name for each single age), because an age isn't a birth year.

Not in the time machine (no official yearly newborn file): India, China, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Germany as a whole (national rankings come from private researchers), Belgium (CAPTCHA). Spain and Italy publish rankings or lookups only.

## 🏰 Medieval names

Names used in England, France and Scandinavia between about 1050 and 1500, kept in their medieval spelling (Aliénor, Hawise, Drogo, Ælfric, Sigríðr). Built by `python3 scripts/build_medieval.py` into `data/medieval-names.json` (3,120 names). Downloads are cached in `raw/medieval/`.

| Source | What it gives | Names | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wiktionary** | every entry in the Middle English, Old French, Middle French, Old English, Old Norse and Old Swedish male/female given-name categories, with the etymology, meaning and (for Norse names) the modern form | 1,346 | CC BY-SA 4.0 |
| **Domesday Book (1086)** | every landholder named in 1066 and 1086, from the Hull Domesday Project data by Prof. J.J.N. Palmer, as listed on opendomesday.org | 1,634 | CC BY-NC-SA |
| **Wikidata** | given names of people born 1050–1500 in the Kingdom of England, the Kingdom of France or the Duchy of Normandy, with the century of the earliest one | 375 | CC0 |

| Culture | Names |
|---|---|
| Medieval English | 1,095 |
| Old English | 1,040 |
| Anglo-Norman | 538 |
| Old French (incl. Middle French) | 270 |
| Old Norse (149 Old Norse + 28 Old Swedish) | 177 |

- A Domesday name held mostly after the Conquest is counted as **Anglo-Norman** (Drogo, Ivo, Warin); one held mostly in 1066 is **Old English** when Wiktionary lists it, otherwise **Medieval English**.
- Old Norse names keep their letters (Þorsteinn, Ingibjǫrg) and give the modern form when Wiktionary has one (Sigríðr → Sigrid). Wiktionary has no Old Icelandic, Old Danish or Old Norwegian given-name categories.
- Wiktionary has no Anglo-Norman given-name categories, so Anglo-Norman names come from Domesday and Wikidata.
- ⚠️ The Domesday data is **non-commercial** (CC BY-NC-SA). Fine for a portfolio; not if Lullabyte ever makes money.
- Not used: the *Dictionary of Medieval Names from European Sources* (dmnes.org). It shows "© 2015–2023 The Editors" and has no open license. Behind the Name and similar sites are also not used.

## ✝️ More biblical and Christian names

Built by `python3 scripts/build_bible_extra.py` into `data/bible-extra.json` (571 rows, same row format as `scripture-names.json`). Downloads are cached in `raw/bible-extra/`.

| Source | What it gives | Rows | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wikipedia, List of biblical names starting with A … Z** | biblical people we didn't have, mostly King James spellings and second names (Abram, Cephas, Dorcas, Hadassah), each checked against STEPBible TIPNR; plus meanings for names we had without one | 285 new · 29 meanings | CC BY-SA 4.0 |
| **Wikidata** | the people on that list that TIPNR doesn't know, kept only when Wikidata calls them a human biblical figure and gives their sex (Barjesus, Benoni, Yehezkel) | 22 | CC0 |
| **STEPBible TIPNR** | KJV, ESV and NIV spellings of well-known people that the Wikipedia list leaves out (Elisabeth, Rebecca, Marcus, Josias) | 65 | CC BY 4.0 |
| **Wikipedia, Virtue name** | Puritan and Christian virtue names (Grace, Faith, Felicity, Prudence, Verity, Gloria) | 32 | CC BY-SA 4.0 |
| **Wikidata (saints) + Wikipedia (titles of Mary)** | names of widely venerated saints, each saint checked on Wikidata (Clare, Augustine, Bernadette, Gerard), and names from titles of the Virgin Mary (Stella, Dolores, Carmen) | 130 saints · 9 Marian and other | CC0 · CC BY-SA 4.0 |
| **Wiktionary** | meanings of the virtue and saints' names, from each English entry's etymology | (meanings) | CC BY-SA 4.0 |

- Only personal names of people from the Wikipedia list get in. Places, peoples, books, titles and epithets are left out (Abana, Philippi, Galilee, Genesis, Caesar, Iscariot, Boanerges). If neither TIPNR nor Wikidata gives a person's sex, the name is left out instead of guessed.
- Christian names that aren't biblical have `texts` set to `""` (never "Bible"), and the story says where the name comes from: a virtue word, a saint, or a title of Mary. Saints whose stories are close to the Bible say so plainly: Anne and Joachim come from the Gospel of James, Dismas from later tradition, Raphael from the Book of Tobit (Catholic and Orthodox Bibles only).
- Not used: Pinterest, FirstCry, parentalquestions.com and other baby-name sites.

## 📖 Meanings and nicknames from Wiktionary

`scripts/fetch_meanings.py` (`python3 scripts/fetch_meanings.py`, add `--cap 0` for no cap) reads English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0) through the MediaWiki API: 50 titles a request, a contact user agent, maxlag, a pause between requests, retries with backoff. Pages are cached in `raw/wikt-meanings/`, so a rerun takes under a minute.

- **Which names:** every single-word name held by 500+ people in `names-db.tsv`, every culture or scripture name with no meaning, and a list of well-known names we knew were missing one. Names that already have a meaning (in `names.js` or the culture files) are skipped. There are 70,041 candidates. The run covers the 15,000 most-held of them plus the must-have list.
- **`data/meanings.json`** `{name: {m, ety, root, src, via?}}` has 4,377 names with a meaning and 1,266 with only an etymology. The meaning is always a gloss Wiktionary gives: the `meaning=` of the given-name template, a "literally"/"meaning" quote, or the gloss on the word the name comes from. Glosses hedged with "possibly", "folk etymology", "compare" or "two unrelated names" are not used. `via` means the meaning comes from the page of the name it derives from: Lev from Лев, Tilly from Matilda, Zofia from Sophie. If Wiktionary has no gloss, `m` is left empty.
- **`data/relations.json`** `[name, relation, related, language, native?]` has 14,474 rows: cognate, variant, diminutive, feminine_form, masculine_form and short_form. They come from the template fields (`dimof=`, `varof=`, `eq=`, `m=`, `f=`), from "diminutive of" and "short for" lines, from "Alternative forms", and from same-language doublets. The optional 5th column holds the pair in its own script when one side isn't Latin, e.g. `["Kostas","short_form","Konstantinos","Greek",["Κώστας","Κωνσταντίνος"]]`. Greek covers 269 rows from every page in Wiktionary's Greek given-name and diminutive categories. Greek Latin spellings are our own passport-style transliteration (Γιάννης → Giannis). Other scripts use Wiktionary's `xlit=`.
- **Not used:** Behind the Name, Nameberry, The Bump or any other commercial name site. Wikidata wasn't needed.

## 📜 Official name lists (approved, recognised, registered)

Government lists that say a first name is **approved**, **recognised**, **registered** or **used** in a country. Built by `python3 scripts/build_name_lists.py` (add `--offline` to reuse the downloads) into `data/name-lists.tsv`: one row per name, sex and list, with the columns `name gender list country count region native status name_type`. `count` is empty when a list has no counts (never 0). `status` is `rejected` only for names Iceland's naming committee turned down, and the site must never suggest those. Hungarian minority-name equivalents and transcriptions go to `data/name-list-relations.tsv`. Downloads are cached in `raw/official-lists/`.

| List | Publisher | What it means | Rows | License / reuse terms | Years |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dk-approved` | Familieretshuset (Agency of Family Law), Denmark | **Approved**: may be given as a first name without an application (girls 28,054, boys 22,607, unisex 1,581) | 52,242 | Reuse allowed if you make clear the presentation is your own version, not Familieretshuset's official lists, and you reference the official lists (familieretshuset.dk/emner/navne/navnelister/godkendte-fornavne). Our presentation is our own. | current list (fetched Oct 2026) |
| `cz-recognised` | Ministerstvo vnitra (Ministry of the Interior), Czechia, Seznam jmen | **Recognised**: names that really exist, in correct spelling; a registry office records them without further checks (male, female, gender-neutral) | 11,509 | Published as open data (CSV); no license named on the page | as of 31 May 2026 |
| `be-population` | Statbel, Belgium: first names of the total population by municipality | **Population**: people living in Belgium with that first name, with Flanders / Wallonia / Brussels totals; names under 5 per municipality are not published | 13,714 | Statbel open data (attribution) | 1 Jan 2025 |
| `cy-births` | Ministry of Interior, Cyprus (data.gov.cy), list of births and names | **Registered births**: everyone in the population register, born 1800–2016, by first name, sex and district | 52,401 | CC BY 4.0 | extract of 25 Oct 2016 |
| `fi-population` | DVV (Digital and Population Data Services Agency), Finland, etunimitilasto | **Population**: living Finnish citizens bearing the name in any position. Names with fewer than 5 bearers are left out for privacy. | 25,350 | CC BY 4.0 | 4 Aug 2026 |
| `hu-legal` | HUN-REN/ELTE Nyelvtudományi Kutatóközpont, Hungary (= 10/2025 (IX. 3.) KIM regulation) | **Approved**: the legal register; only these names can be registered | 4,703 | Legislation, not under copyright in Hungary | list of 31 Jul 2025 |
| `hu-minority-<language>` (13 lists) | Hungary, 11–23/2025 (IX. 3.) KIM regulations, Magyar Közlöny 2025/101 | **Approved for nationality communities**: Armenian, Bulgarian, Croatian, German, Greek, Polish, Roma, Romanian, Rusyn, Serbian, Slovak, Slovene, Ukrainian. `native` = original-script form | 12,026 | Legislation, not under copyright in Hungary | 3 Sep 2025 |
| `is-approved` / `is-rejected` / `is-pending` | Registers Iceland (Þjóðskrá, via island.is), Personal Names Register | **Approved / rejected / pending** decisions of the Personal Names Committee; `name_type` = first or middle | 5,164 / 607 / 1 | Public register; no license stated | current (fetched Oct 2026) |
| `pt-admitted` | IRN (Instituto dos Registos e do Notariado), Portugal, Lista Nomes Próprios | **Admitted**: names accepted by the Portuguese civil registry. The PDF has no "não admitidos" (refused) section. | 7,481 | Public administrative document; no license stated | June 2021 |
| `ro-registered` | DGEP (Direcția Generală pentru Evidența Persoanelor), Romania, name-day press releases | **Registered**: people currently in the population register (never babies born in a year). Counts with dates also go to `data/census-names.json`. | 316 | Public press releases; no license stated | 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023 |

**The rule:** approved in a country ≠ used in a country ≠ originating there. Denmark approving "Olatunji" or Portugal admitting "Aditi" says nothing about where the name comes from, and a population count is not a newborn count.

- **Spellings are kept exactly.** Czech diacritics (Jiří, Štěpán, Kateřina; the ministry prints names in capitals, so we only change the case), Icelandic letters (Þór, Guðrún, Ólöf), Hungarian (László, Zsuzsanna) and Portuguese (Ágata and Agata are separate entries). Romanian names keep the cedilla ş/ţ where DGEP printed it (53 names); search folding treats ş and ș alike. Entries like "Georgică/Georgica" share one count, so `name-lists.tsv` lists each spelling with an empty count; `census-names.json` keeps the printed string and its count.
- **Cyprus:** the register prints Greek names in capitals without accents. `native` keeps that form. `name` is the Ministry of Interior's own romanisation table (`Τυποποίηση Ελληνικών Ονομάτων` on data.gov.cy) where it has the name, otherwise ELOT 743, which matches that table on 1,008 of its 1,010 entries. Names given in the Latin alphabet (Turkish Cypriot and foreign names) have no `native`. Placeholders such as "-" or "ΝΕΚΡΟ" (dead) are dropped. The current dataset resource holds surnames only; the first-name file is `openData25102016.dsv`.
- **Hungarian minority registers** are parsed from the Magyar Közlöny PDF, and every table's rows are checked against its row numbers. Cells that list several variants ("Bratován, Brátán") become one row each. Latin look-alike letters inside Cyrillic or Greek words are corrected (about 1,200), and so are Greek or Armenian look-alikes inside Latin names. A handful of Ukrainian Cyrillic forms are encoded in the PDF as Latin look-alikes and may still read oddly.
- **Belgium** is now ingested: statbel.fgov.be still blocks downloads, so the files are the Internet Archive's byte-for-byte captures of Statbel's official `TA_POP_MALE_2025.xlsx` / `TA_POP_FEMALE_2025.xlsx`.
- **Romania:** only the 11 DGEP releases with a real text layer are used. The other 63 name-day releases (most of 2020–2023, including Maria and Ion) are scanned images, and OCR cannot reproduce ş/ţ/ș/ț exactly. No 2024–2026 releases are on depabd.mai.gov.ro. `scripts/build_years.py` rewrites `data/census-names.json`, so run `build_name_lists.py` after it to put the Romania rows back.
- **Iceland:** 43 entries hidden on island.is and one with no status are skipped. Some names were both rejected and later approved, so they appear in both lists.
- **Not used:** forebears.io or any commercial name site (their terms forbid reuse and their counts are estimates).

**Meanings from the name in its own script.** `scripts/fetch_native_meanings.py` (`python3 scripts/fetch_native_meanings.py`) handles the 3,849 culture rows that have no meaning, say "Written <native>." and have no meaning in `data/meanings.json`, because Wiktionary has no page for the Latin spelling. It reads the native-script page in English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0), only in the row's own language section, with the same polite settings as `fetch_meanings.py`. Pages and transliterations are cached in `raw/wikt-native/`. A meaning is kept only when Wiktionary states it: the page has a given-name sense and the same etymology defines the word (आभा "lustre"), or glosses its source word (Софья ← Greek "wisdom"); or the page says it is the feminine form of a word that is defined (Suhani: सुहानी is the feminine of सुहाना "pleasant, agreeable, nice"); or the name line gives the meaning. Compounds count only when every part is glossed (Айдос "moon + friend"), so a half meaning is never shown. The reading follows a word's own line of descent ("from", "the feminine of") and stops at "a derivative of", "akin to", "see", "cognate", "possibly", "folk etymology" or "compare". Case forms are never followed (В'ячеслава is also the genitive of В'ячеслав), and neither is a form-of under another etymology (سورنا is the name Surena and a spelling of "zurna"). The result is `data/native-meanings.json` (341 names, same `{m, ety, root, src, via}` shape, with `via` = the native word). The other rows stay empty because the page gives no gloss: most say only "from Arabic" or "from Sanskrit", or the page doesn't exist.

## Russia: Moscow's newborn names, the peoples of the Russian Federation, and Latin spellings

Where a name is used (Moscow's registry) and where it comes from (a people and its language) are kept apart: a name registered in Moscow is not thereby a Russian name, and a Tatar name used in Moscow is still a Tatar name.

**Moscow (time machine).** The Moscow Government open data portal publishes two datasets from the Moscow civil registry (Управление ЗАГС города Москвы): `2009` "Сведения о наиболее популярных женских именах среди новорожденных" (girls) and `2011` "… мужских именах …" (boys), one row per name per month since 2015 (Name, NumberOfPersons, Year, Month). They are **thresholded, not complete**: each month lists only that month's 100 most popular names, so a year (the twelve months added up) counts a name only for the months it made the top 100. License: data.mos.ru's terms say everything on the portal is open data under Russian Government decree No. 583 of 10 July 2013 and may be reproduced without limits, with a link to the portal. `python3 scripts/fetch_moscow_names.py` downloads them into `raw/ru/moscow-names-(2009|2011).(json|csv|zip)`; the portal answers only from Russia, so from elsewhere export them by hand (Export → JSON or CSV on data.mos.ru/opendata/2009 and /2011) or set `MOS_API_KEY` for apidata.mos.ru. `build_years.py` adds the place `ru-moscow` ("Moscow (city)", group Russia) as soon as both files are there: names in Cyrillic as registered, a `latin` map with each name's BGN/PCGN spelling for search, and a year left out until all twelve months are published. **Not in `years.json` yet**: the files couldn't be downloaded from here.

**Cultures within the Russian Federation.** `python3 scripts/fetch_russia_names.py` then `python3 scripts/build_russia_cultures.py` → `data/russia-cultures.json`, in the row format of `culture-names.json`.

| Source | What it gives |
|---|---|
| **Wiktionary** (CC BY-SA 4.0) | every page under "<Language> given names" and its subcategories (male, female, unisex, "from Arabic", diminutives) for Russian, Tatar, Bashkir, Chuvash, Mari, Udmurt, Komi, Erzya, Moksha, Chechen, Ingush, Avar, Dargwa, Lezgi, Lak, Tabasaran, Kumyk, Nogai, Adyghe, Kabardian, Karachay-Balkar, Ossetian, Kalmyk, Buryat, Yakut, Tuvan, Altai, Khakas, Shor, Nenets, Khanty, Mansi, Evenki, Even and Chukchi. A Russian entry that says the name comes from one of these languages (Шойгу, from Tuvan) also counts for that people. Cached in `raw/ru/wikt/`. |
| **Wikidata** (CC0) | given-name items (P31 Q202444, Q11879590, Q12308941, Q3409032) whose "language of work or name" (P407) is one of these languages, with the native label (P1705). Cached in `raw/ru/wikidata-given-names.json`. |

One culture per people (Tatar, Bashkir, Avar, Dargin, Lezgin, Sakha…), never a region or a country; Karachay-Balkar stays one label because the sources don't say which of the two peoples a name belongs to. A name shared by several peoples has one row per culture. The native spelling is kept as "Written <native>." (Tatar and Bashkir ә ө ү, Sakha ҕ ҥ ө ү һ, Chechen and Avar Ӏ, Buryat ү ө һ, Ossetian æ) and the name is its Latin form: Wikidata's English label, or a letter-by-letter Latin spelling of the language's Cyrillic. Religion is filled only where the entry states it. Left out, and counted by the script: a name whose source says it came from Russian; a Wikidata language tag on a name Wiktionary lists as Russian (Сергей tagged Yakut, Chechen and Bashkir) and a Wikidata Russian tag on another people's name (Алсу), since those tags record where a spelling is used, not where the name is from; names whose sex isn't given. Most of these languages have no given-name pages on Wiktionary and few tagged items on Wikidata, so the file is small outside Russian and Bashkir.

**Latin spellings of Russian names.** `python3 scripts/build_russia_forms.py` → `data/russia-forms.json`, rows `[cyrillic, [{"latin", "system"}, …]]` for every Russian given name on Wiktionary. Generated letter by letter from the Cyrillic (`scripts/russian_latin.py`): **BGN/PCGN** 1947 (strict, with ’ ” and the separating dot; and the same without its marks), **ISO 9**:1995, the **scientific** transliteration, and **ICAO passport 2013** (ICAO Doc 9303 as used in Russian passports since 2014: Наталья → Natalia, Юлия → Iuliia). From Wiktionary: the transliterations the entry lists (`xlit=`, "common"), the English entries that render the name ("English renderings of Russian … given names": Sergei, Yevgeny, Artyom, "common"), and the entry's English equivalent (`eq=`): "conventional English" when it is a spelling of the same name (Alexander), "English equivalent" when it is a different name (Сергей eq=Sergius, Евгений eq=Eugene). The script also appends `romanization_variant` rows to `data/relations.json` (`[latin, "romanization_variant", other latin, "Russian", [cyrillic, cyrillic]]`), one per pair of plain-letter spellings of the same Cyrillic name (Sergey, Sergei, Sergej), keeping every existing row and replacing only its own rows on a rerun.


## More real names: data/names-extra.tsv

`python3 scripts/build_names_extra.py` (add `--offline` to use only what is already in `raw/`) writes `data/names-extra.tsv`, in the same format as `names-db.tsv` (name, gender f/m/u/?, countries, people recorded). It holds only names whose folded form (lowercase, accents removed, spaces and hyphens removed, as `fold()` in app.js) is **not** already in `names-db.tsv`. Every name is printed by its source; nothing is generated. The cleaning matches `build_world.py`: Latin script only, at least one vowel, no placeholders (Sin nombre, NN, Ignorado, Sans prénom…), no digits, no letter three times in a row, 2 to 20 letters. All-caps sources are title-cased, and accents are kept as the source prints them. Compound given names are split into single names ("María del Carmen" becomes María and Carmen). Particles and the joining words of devotional names (de, del, la, los, y, da, dos, san, santa, sagrado, corazón, dios…) are dropped. When the same folded name comes from several sources, the spelling with the most people is kept.

Gender comes from the people a source records by sex: f or m when 80% or more are one sex, u otherwise. Sources with no counts (approved lists, Wikidata, JMnedict, Wiktionary) give their class. Names only Argentina records (it has no sex column) stay "?". "People recorded" is 0 for names that come only from lists without counts.

| Order | Source | Licence / where | New names |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **RENAPER (Argentina)**, historical names 1922–2015, counts summed over the years; code `ar` | datos.gob.ar; `raw/ar-renaper-historico-nombres-1922-2015.zip` | 96,675 |
| 2 | **Official name lists** in `data/name-lists.tsv` (rejected Icelandic names skipped); its own country codes | see the section above | 45,570 |
| 3 | **IBGE (Brazil)**: Censo 2010 names (brasil.io's mirror of the IBGE API) and the **Censo 2022 names API** (`servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/v3/nomes/2022`, every name with 20+ people, by sex, about 4,500 pages fetched half a second apart). Per name and sex the larger of the two counts is kept; code `br` | `raw/br-nomes.csv.gz`, `raw/br-ibge-2022/` | 22,480 |
| 4 | **Registro Civil (Chile)**, every name 1920–2021; code `cl` | `raw/cl.csv` | 489 |
| 5 | **Wikidata** (CC0): items that are a given name (Q202444, Q11879590 female, Q12308941 male, Q3409032 unisex), with every Latin-script label in any language, aliases and native label (P1705). Queried by class and item-number range, and a range is split in two when the answer gets cut off; code `wd` | `raw/wd-given-names-latin/` | 41,125 |
| 6 | **JMnedict** (EDRDG, CC BY-SA 4.0): the romanised reading of given-name entries (fem/masc/given); code `jp` | `raw/JMnedict.xml.gz` | 22,658 (almost all already in the Japanese storied list) |
| 7 | **INSEE (France), fichier des personnes décédées**, everyone who died in France from 1970 to 2025, with every given name each person had (Licence Ouverte). The yearly files total about 6 GB, so each is read once as it downloads and only its name counts are kept; code `fr` | data.gouv.fr; `raw/fr-deces/deces-YYYY.tsv` | 151,790 |
| 8 | **Wiktionary** (CC BY-SA 4.0): the titles of every entry in a "<language> given names" category and its subcategories (male, female, unisex, diminutives, renderings), in every language. The "from <language>" origin subcategories are skipped because nearly all their entries are already in the plain category. One request a second; code `wikt` | `raw/wikt-given-names.tsv` | 7,860 |

Result: **388,647** names in `names-extra.tsv` (6.2 MB). There are **922,965** distinct real names: `names-db.tsv` has 511,117 folded names, `names-extra.tsv` adds 388,647, and the storied lists (scripture, bible-extra, cultures, also-cultures, East Asian, medieval, Azerbaijan, Hebrew, Russia) add another 23,201 that are in neither file (their total is 94,816). The "new" counts above are measured against `names-db.tsv`. The JMnedict names were mostly in the storied lists already, so they add only 384 to the total.

**Checked and not used:** the IBGE Censo 2010 ranking API (it returns only the top 20 per query; brasil.io holds the full list), IBGE's per-state 2022 lists (same 20-person threshold, so nothing new), Wikidata lexemes (603 lemmas), Scotland's NRS list (102 new), Ecuador INEC (search tool only, no download), Czech MV name frequencies (the site blocks downloads), and Forebears and other commercial name sites (not allowed).

## Georgian, Albanian, Pashto and San Marino: data/caucasus-balkan-names.json

`python3 scripts/build_caucasus_balkan.py` → `data/caucasus-balkan-names.json`, in the row format of `culture-names.json`. Downloads are cached in `raw/caucasus-balkan/` (delete a file to fetch it again). A name is written only when it is not already in `culture-names.json` with the same culture. Culture, sex and meaning come only from what a source states. A name with no sex in any source is left out.

| Source | What it gives |
|---|---|
| **English Wiktionary** (CC BY-SA 4.0) | every page under "Georgian/Albanian/Pashto male/female given names" and their subcategories. The category gives the sex. The entry gives the meaning: `meaning=`, `lit=`, or the gloss in the first sentence of the etymology ("From {{m\|sq\|shpresë\|\|hope}}"). A sentence that starts with "perhaps", "possibly" or "probably" is not used, and only the etymology that holds the given-name sense counts (მაშა "pliers" is a different word from the name Masha). |
| **Georgian Wiktionary** (CC BY-SA 4.0) | "მამაკაცის სახელი (ქართული)" (35 male) and "ქალის სახელი (ქართული)" (9 female). Used only for the name and its sex: the pages define the ordinary Georgian word, in Georgian. |
| **Albanian Wiktionary** | has no given-name category ("Emra shqip" means "Albanian nouns"), and the must-check names (Drita, Besa, Ylli…) have no pages. Nothing used. |
| **Pashto Wiktionary** | has no given-name category ("پښتو نومونه" means Pashto nouns, 2 pages). Nothing used. |
| **Wikidata** (CC0) | given-name items (P31 Q202444, Q11879590, Q12308941, Q3409032) whose P407 is Georgian (Q8108), Albanian (Q8748) or Pashto (Q58680), or whose native label (P1705) is tagged ka/sq or written in Mkhedruli. The class gives the sex. Items also tagged Mingrelian or Svan are left out. Pashto items count only when Pashto is their only P407 and they have a Pashto-script native label. |

**Georgian** names are spelled in Latin with the 2002 national romanization, without its apostrophes (ქ and კ are both k, თ/ტ t, ფ/პ p, ც/წ ts, ჩ/ჭ ch, ყ q, ღ gh, ხ kh, ჟ zh, ჯ j). The Mkhedruli spelling is kept as "Written <native>." so that `build_native_forms.py`, which now also reads this file, picks it up. Sources write some names in the nominative (დავითი) and some bare (დავით). When both forms appear, they are merged into the bare form (Davit), which is how Georgians write their names in Latin. A nominative-only form is never cut down, because Giorgi and Irakli also end in -i. **Albanian** names keep ë and ç.

**Pashtun** (language Pashto) counts only names whose own entry makes them Pashto: no "borrowed from Arabic/Persian", no source language in the given-name line. It can be a Pashto compound (اباسین Abasin "father + Sindh") or a Pashto word that the page also gives as a name (هېلۍ "duck"). Wiktionary has common-noun pages for سپوږمۍ "moon", لمر "sun", اتل "hero" and زمری "lion", but none of them gives a given-name sense, so they are not added. khyber.org's Pashto names list has no stated licence and the host did not resolve, so it was not used.

**San Marino.** These are the given names (P735) of the 902 Captains Regent on Wikidata (P39 = Q258045). All 292 one-word given names are already in our data (`names-db.tsv`, `names-extra.tsv` or a storied list), so the file gains no new rows from them. The 6 that remain are compound names (Gian Carlo, Pier Paolo, Marc'Antonio…). The statistics office (statistica.sm, UPECEDS) publishes no first-name table. Its "Curiosità" page gives only a few top names in its text (December 2025 residents: Andrea, Marco, Maria, Sara, Giulia; 2025 births: Edoardo, Leonardo, Samuele, Damiano, Camilla, Matilde).

**Not available:** Geostat (geostat.ge, reachable) publishes no baby-name table or download. INSTAT Albania (instat.gov.al, reachable) publishes births by prefecture and municipality but not by name.
